Issue title: Managed Dolt dies ~15s after the agent session that restarted it closes: the orphan sweep reaps the scope watchdog as that session's process-table root

## Summary

A managed Dolt server that `gc dolt restart` (or any auto-ensure start) brings up from inside an agent session dies about 15 seconds after that session closes. The scope watchdog and the `dolt sql-server` inherit the shell's `GC_SESSION_ID`, the watchdog reparents to init, and the session reconciler's process-table orphan sweep reaps it as that session's orphan once the session bead is closed. The watchdog's SIGTERM handler takes the server down with it. Whichever `gc` or `bd` command restarts Dolt next runs inside another session, so the new watchdog carries that session's id and the trap re-arms.

Measured on gc v1.4.1 ([`58ef17e3`](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/58ef17e3)) on 2026-09-12; the code is unchanged on `main` at [`835718da`](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/commit/835718da0677d21ca8bc3e28ce51a556930fb2cf).

## Timeline

| Time (UTC) | Event | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 17:13:09 | Agent session A ran `gc dolt restart` from its own shell. New watchdog and server started. | dolt.log `Starting server` |
| 17:25:08 | Session A stopped. | events log `session.stopped` |
| 17:25:17 | The reconciler reaped the watchdog session A had started; Dolt died the same second. | journal: `session reconciler: reaped process-table orphan pid=1255869 session=<A>`; dolt.log: `gc scope watchdog: received terminated; terminating dolt sql-server pid 1255878` |
| 17:25:21 | Controller-wide circuit breaker open: `buildDesiredState ... scale_check failed`, order dispatch `bd list` failures. | supervisor journal |
| 17:25:23 | Dolt restarted by an auto-ensure path inside agent session B, which had just woken. The new watchdog carried session B's id. | dolt.log `Starting server` 7 s before B's first mail |
| 17:35:46 | Session B stopped. | `session.stopped` |
| 17:36:04 | Reaped again (`pid=1339990 session=<B>`); Dolt pid 1339999 died; a fresh session's first `bd show` failed with `connection refused` and tripped the breaker. | journal, dolt.log |
| 17:36:07 | The supervisor restarted Dolt. This watchdog has no `GC_SESSION_ID` in `/proc/<pid>/environ` and its POSIX session is `gc supervisor run`. It survived every later session stop, which is the stable state. | `ps -o sess`, `/proc/<pid>/environ` |

Control: a third session that stopped at 17:31:33 bounced nothing, because Dolt was not stamped with its id.

## Mechanism

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Agent shell runs gc dolt restart] --> B[Watchdog and server inherit the shell's session id]
    B --> C[Agent session closes]
    C --> D[Reconciler sweeps roots whose session bead is closed]
    D --> E[Watchdog killed, server terminated]
    E --> F[Next gc or bd command from any session restarts Dolt]
    F --> B
```

- [`doltServerEnv`](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/blob/835718da0677d21ca8bc3e28ce51a556930fb2cf/cmd/gc/dolt_start_managed.go#L1262) passes `os.Environ()` through unchanged apart from `DOLT_DISABLE_EVENT_FLUSH`, and both the watchdog spawn ([dolt_scope_watchdog.go:141](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/blob/835718da0677d21ca8bc3e28ce51a556930fb2cf/cmd/gc/dolt_scope_watchdog.go#L141)) and the server spawn inside the watchdog ([dolt_scope_watchdog.go:214](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/blob/835718da0677d21ca8bc3e28ce51a556930fb2cf/cmd/gc/dolt_scope_watchdog.go#L214)) use it. A restart from an agent shell therefore stamps both processes with `GC_SESSION_ID`, `GC_SESSION_NAME`, `GC_AGENT` and the rest of the session's identity.
- [`sweepProcessTableOrphans`](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/blob/835718da0677d21ca8bc3e28ce51a556930fb2cf/cmd/gc/session_beads.go#L3218) asks the scanner for every process-tree root carrying a `GC_SESSION_ID` and terminates any whose session bead is closed. The watchdog reparents to init on purpose, so [`isRootWithSessionID`](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/blob/835718da0677d21ca8bc3e28ce51a556930fb2cf/internal/runtime/proctable/scan_linux.go#L169) reports it as a root.
- The watchdog's [signal handler](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/blob/835718da0677d21ca8bc3e28ce51a556930fb2cf/cmd/gc/dolt_scope_watchdog.go#L252) forwards the SIGTERM to the server, which is the behaviour a deleted scope needs and the wrong one here.

This is the same shape as #5392, where the tmux server inherited the founding session's id and was reported as a root. The difference is that the watchdog is a `gc` re-exec, so it cannot be excluded by `comm` the way the tmux server was: marking it infrastructure would promote its `dolt sql-server` child to a root through the parent-is-infrastructure rule, and [`LiveRuntime`](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/blob/835718da0677d21ca8bc3e28ce51a556930fb2cf/internal/runtime/runtime.go#L387) carries no argv for the sweep to test.

## Proposed fix

Strip the per-session identity keys in `doltServerEnv`, so neither the watchdog nor the server ever carries a `GC_SESSION_ID` and the sweep has nothing to attribute. A managed server is city infrastructure, not part of any session; the supervisor-started watchdog that survived the incident already has this shape. The key set is what [`session.RuntimeEnvWithSessionContext`](https://github.com/gastownhall/gascity/blob/835718da0677d21ca8bc3e28ce51a556930fb2cf/internal/session/lifecycle.go#L67) injects, plus `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`.

PR to follow.
